onboardingCloseAfter: Reading list is closed in Firefox and its entry has been removed from the tree.
onboardingCloseBefore: Reading list is live. Hover over its row to reveal the × (Delete) button.
onboardingCloseDelete: Save closes a tab and keeps its entry. Closing in Firefox follows your save-on-close settings. Delete removes the tree entry and closes the tab if it is open. For actions on a parent tab or note, Settings → Context Menu lets you include unselected child items always, only when collapsed, or never. A window includes its contents.
onboardingCloseDescription: Click the × (Delete) button on a tab or window row to close it in Firefox and remove its entry from the tree. Deleting a window also removes its contents. Use Save if you want to close the window or tab in the browser but save it in the tree.
onboardingCloseWindowAfter: Research window is closed in Firefox and its entries have been removed from the tree. Planning window stays open.
onboardingCloseWindowBefore: Research window is open. Its × (Delete) button closes the window and removes its contents from the tree.
onboardingCollapsedCount: When a tab or note is collapsed, the number on the left replaces the expand/collapse arrow while you are not hovering over it. It counts all child items underneath that branch, including nested children. Hover to see the arrow again, then click it to expand the branch.
onboardingContainersCaption: Research uses Work, Reading list uses Personal, and Project overview uses no container. The live state dots stay blue in every container.
onboardingContainersDescription: Firefox containers keep browsing identities separate. A container tab shows its colored indicator and container icon; hover the row to see its name. These marks describe its container, independently of its state or indentation. Change the color treatment and icon position in Settings → Containers.
onboardingContainersHidden: Your settings currently hide container colors or icons.
onboardingDemoSafe: This is a sample tree. Your tabs stay as they are.
onboardingDropPosition: Choose where to drop the item
onboardingError: Something could not be saved or opened. Please try again.
onboardingExampleLabel: Example tree with windows, tabs, notes, separators, and a collapsed branch
onboardingFinishDescription: Automatic snapshots are on by default and keep copies of your tree on this device. In Settings → Storage you can review, restore, import, or export sessions. Export a copy if you need a backup outside this Firefox profile.
onboardingFocusAfter: Research is now active. A colored outline marks its row.
onboardingFocusBefore: Research is live, but is not the active tab in its window.
onboardingFocusDescription: Double-click a live tab in the tree to focus it in Firefox. Double-click an unloaded tab to load and focus it. These are the default actions; you can change them in settings.
onboardingImportDescription: Choose a Session Flow, Tabs Outliner, Tab Session Manager, or Session Buddy file. Review it before restoring tabs.
onboardingLabelsAfter: The tab label appears beside its page title; a window title replaces its displayed name.
onboardingLabelsBefore: Choose Tab or Window to see its editor. Right-click Research or the window row to try the same controls yourself.
onboardingLabelsDescription: Right-click a single tab and choose Edit Label, enter a label, then choose OK. The label appears before the page title; clear it to remove it. For a window, choose Edit Title to change its displayed name. These change the labels in your tree without renaming the webpage.
onboardingMultiSelectAfter: The highlighted rows are selected. Ctrl-click toggles individual items; Shift-click selects a range in tree order.
onboardingMultiSelectBefore: Choose an example, then watch the selected rows highlight. You can also try Ctrl-click, Shift-click, and right-click on these sample rows.
onboardingMultiSelectDescription: Ctrl-click to add or remove individual items from your selection (Cmd on macOS). Click an item, then Shift-click another to select the range between them, including hidden child items. Drag a selected item to move the selection together, or right-click a selected item to act on the selection. Windows carry their contents; actions on collapsed tabs or notes can include hidden children. Change drag selection and child handling in Settings → Drag and Drop, and child handling for each menu action in Settings → Context Menu.
onboardingNoteAddAfter: A new note now sits outside the windows. Continue to learn how to edit its text.
onboardingNoteAddBefore: The Add note button in the toolbar creates a note at the root of the tree.
onboardingNoteAddDescription: Click Add note in the toolbar to create a note outside of windows. Right-click an item and choose Add Note to add a note beneath that item.
onboardingNoteEditAfter: The note text has changed. Notes can be used as labels to organize window contents and as groups to organize windows.
onboardingNoteEditBefore: Double-click New note to open the same text editor used in the tree.
onboardingNoteEditDescription: Double-click a note to change its text, then choose OK. You can also right-click it and choose Edit Note.
onboardingNoteGroupAfter: Both windows now belong to Projects. Try the arrow to collapse or expand the group.
onboardingNoteGroupBefore: Projects is a note outside the windows. Windows can be nested under it.
onboardingNoteGroupDescription: Drop a window onto the middle of a note to indent it underneath as a child. Add more windows under the same note to keep a group together. Use the expand/collapse arrow to collapse or expand the group.
onboardingOpenAfter: Reading list is now open in Firefox. Its live dot and colored outline show that it is loaded and active.
onboardingOpenBefore: Reading list is saved in the tree and closed in Firefox.
onboardingOpenDescription: Double-click a saved tab to open it in Firefox. A saved tab is kept in the tree without an open browser tab. Double-click an unloaded tab to load and focus its page.
onboardingOpenTabsDescription: Start with your current windows and tabs.
onboardingOrganizeAfter: Reading list is now indented under Research as a child item. Try the expand/collapse arrow to collapse or expand the branch.
onboardingOrganizeBefore: Research and Reading list are separate tabs in the same window.
onboardingOrganizeDescription: Drop an item onto the middle of another item to nest it underneath, indented as a child item. Drop above or below to make it a sibling item at the same indent level. Use the expand/collapse arrow to collapse or expand a branch. Moving live tabs can also change their order in Firefox.
onboardingOrganizeSiblingAfter: Reading list is now a sibling of Research at the same indent level.
onboardingPrivateInstructions: To include private windows, enable access in Firefox. Session Flow cannot grant this permission for you.
onboardingPrivateOptional: Private-window access is optional. You can use Session Flow with regular windows and change this later.
onboardingPrivateReload: Firefox reloads Session Flow when you change this permission. If you allow access within the next 30 minutes, this introduction will reopen here automatically with your progress saved.
onboardingReadTreeDescription: The dot and text color tell you whether a tab is live, unloaded, or saved. A colored outline marks the active tab in the focused Firefox window.
onboardingReadyDescription: Open Session Flow whenever you need it from the toolbar. You can close this welcome tab and replay the introduction from Settings → General.
onboardingReplayHint: All preferences can be changed in settings. Find this introduction again under General.
onboardingRetainTreeDescription: Keep private titles and URLs across restarts. Snapshot and favicon retention have separate settings.
onboardingRetainTreeLabel: Keep private windows in the saved tree
onboardingRetentionDescription: Allow private windows in the saved tree and snapshots, and cache their favicons. Titles and URLs can remain on this device after private windows close.
onboardingRetentionNote: Firefox access and data retention are separate choices. With retention off, private windows can appear while open, but are excluded from future tree saves, snapshots, and favicon caching. Existing snapshots are kept until you delete them.
onboardingSaveAfter: Reading list is saved and closed in Firefox. The entry stays in the tree with an amber dot and muted text.
onboardingSaveBefore: Reading list is live in Firefox. The Save button appears when you hover over a real tab row.
onboardingSaveDescription: Click Save on a tab row to close the browser tab and keep its entry in the tree. The Save button on a window row closes the browser window and keeps the window and its tabs in the tree. Double-click a saved tab or window to reopen it.
onboardingSaveWindowAfter: Research window is closed in Firefox. The window and its tabs remain as saved entries in the tree.
onboardingSaveWindowBefore: Research window is open. Hover over its row to reveal the Save button.
onboardingSelectBranchesAfter: Shift selected a range across both windows, including hidden child items. Expanding Related pages reveals that those children are selected too.
onboardingSelectDragAfter: The moved items are now children of Project overview. The source rows stayed in place until the drop.
onboardingSelectMenuAfter: Save closed the selected sample tabs and kept both entries in the tree.
onboardingSelectionDragDisabled: Your settings currently drag only the item under the pointer. Enable including selected items in Drag and Drop settings to move the selection together.
onboardingSettingsDescription: To open Settings later, click the gear button at the bottom right of the session tree. You can also right-click the Session Flow icon in the Firefox toolbar and choose Settings.
onboardingStartDescription: Start with your current tabs, or bring a saved session from another manager. You can import later in Settings → Storage.
onboardingStateActiveDescription: Colored outline: the active tab in the focused Firefox window.
onboardingStateFocusNote: Active describes focus. Live, unloaded, and saved describe the tab’s state; the dot represents that state.
onboardingStateLiveDescription: Filled blue dot and light text: open and loaded in Firefox.
onboardingStateSavedDescription: Small amber dot and warm muted text: kept in the tree, currently closed in Firefox.
onboardingStateUnloadedDescription: Hollow blue dot and muted text: still open, with its page unloaded to save memory.
onboardingTabGroupsCaption: Research and Reading list share the Projects group. Project overview belongs to Reading. Hover their rows to see the group names.
onboardingTabGroupsDescription: Firefox tab groups appear as colored marks on grouped tabs. Hover a row to see its group name. Group membership is separate from the tree’s indentation: tabs can share a Firefox group without being parent and child. Change marker position or visibility in Settings → Tab Groups.
onboardingTabGroupsHidden: Your settings currently hide tab-group color indicators.
onboardingToolbarDescription: Click the Session Flow button in Firefox’s toolbar to open your session tree. If it is not visible, open Extensions (the puzzle-piece button), then open the menu beside Session Flow (gear or three dots) and choose Pin to Toolbar. You can also open Session Flow directly from the Extensions panel.
onboardingWelcomeDescription: Organize your windows and tabs in a vertical tree and keep sessions for later. Windows can contain tabs, notes and separators. Items can be indented and collapsed to better display and keep related pages together. Notes can be placed outside of windows and be used as a parent to store groups of windows.
onboardingWelcomePrivacy: Session Flow has no analytics or tracking and does not send your browsing data to its developer. Your session tree and snapshots are stored locally in your Firefox profile. Website icons may be fetched from the sites that provide them.
onboardingWelcomeReassurance: Your open tabs are already in the tree. This introduction does not close or rearrange them.
onboardingWindowBarCaption: This window has 3 live, 2 unloaded, and 1 saved tab, including an unloaded tab inside the collapsed branch.
onboardingWindowBarDescription: The bar on the right of a window summarizes its tabs, including tabs in collapsed branches. Blue represents live tabs, dim blue unloaded tabs, and amber saved tabs. Each segment’s length reflects the number of tabs in that state. The number beside the bar is the total tab count.
openTabsAndWindowsWillAlsoBeClosedInFire: Open tabs and windows will also be closed in Firefox.
